finding_1_pool_is_stale.conclusion: the pool does not track the world price; it is pinned near one tick while the reference moves ~5x further around it
finding_1_pool_is_stale.note: deviation flips sign with the world price, which is what a stale pool does; it is NOT a persistent one-way premium

finding_2_activity_collapsed.correction: the README figure of '$558/day' is a 50h average. The most recent 24h cleared $135.09 across 12 swaps from 3 addresses. Both are true; the 24h figure is the current state and it is 4x smaller.

finding_3_executable_edge_is_one_way.caveat: gross of exchange taker fees. Gate spot taker is ~20 bp and a CEX->chain round trip also pays a withdrawal, so a +42 bp sell-side advantage does not by itself fund the loop. It is reported because it is the number that shows the pool is mispriced, not because it is harvestable at retail fee tiers.

finding_4_the_gate_cannot_see_this.current_gate: refuses when |spot - own TWAP| < round-trip cost + margin
finding_4_the_gate_cannot_see_this.blind_spot: if the WHOLE pool drifts away from world price, spot and TWAP move together, the measured gap stays ~0, and the vault refuses a trade that an external reference says is actually profitable (or permits none of one that is not)
